_why: One worked example runs through the whole paper: Figure 3, Supplementary Data S1,
Supplementary Figure S3, the Table S11 controlled panel and the Methods narrative, and
Figure 2 panel F draws the same design as an assembled pegRNA.
It installs the PUBLISHED edit at this protospacer, G to T at position 301 (Lin et al.
2021), on the spacer ATTTGGGTATGGTGGTGCAA. Until 20 September 2026 the edit was a
demonstration substitution, G to A at 306, which no study reports; the spacer is
unchanged, so the figures and the interface screenshots keep their subject and only the
substitution moves onto the published one.
On the published edit the interface returns 20 candidate spacers and three tie at the top
composite score -- CAACCAACATTTGGGTATGG, ATTTGGGTATGGTGGTGCAA and TTTGGGTATGGTGGTGCAAT.
This is the second of the three, so it is among the tool's first choices on score rather
than the single highest, and the paper says so wherever it matters. Of the three it
returns the best reverse-transcriptase template (score 99) and a primer-binding site
inside the rice band. The spacer Lin et al. published, GGGTATGGTGGTGCAATGGG, is rank 5 of
20 for this edit and nicks at g.300, which would put the edit at the nick itself; it is
the subject of Supplementary Figure S4 and the head-to-head, not of the worked example.
The search bounds are the tool's own interface defaults (pbs-min 8, pbs-max 17, rt-min 10,
rt-max 30), so the figures state what a reader gets by opening the tool and changing
spacer_note: one of three spacers tied at the top composite score for the published edit at this locus, and the second of the three by sort order -- among the tool’s first choices rather than the single highest. The published protospacer, GGGTATGGTGGTGCAATGGG, is rank 5 of 20 for this edit.
edit_note: the published substitution at this protospacer, G to T at position 301 (Lin et al. 2021); the reference base is read from the sequence at edit_pos0 and is G
locus_note: Two different protospacers in the rice ALS gene were both called OsALS-T2 — one by Lin 2020, one by Lin 2021 — and the site Lin 2021 calls OsALS-T2 is the one Lin 2020 calls OsALS-T1. The labels carry their study so none means two things; see analysis/als_sites.json. sequence_file keeps its original filename.
